name: 托瓦洛·沙嗥
src: 迷宫纪前传/迷宫纪前传时段_四_深井的年月.md:5999
who: Tovalo of the Sand-Howl line, a wolf-eared beastfolk letter courier of the Wind-Chaser tribe on the post road at the edge of the great sand sea, and a legend who once split a standing wall of sand open with a borrowed blade and held the crack for nine days; past seventy but looking twenty-three, as he has since his name was fixed: tall, lean and long-limbed, a runner's build. Short silver-grey hair; silver-grey wolf ears whose tips are black; a silver-grey wolf's tail that streams straight out behind him when he runs. Warm amber eyes. Faint pale sand-scuff lines across the bridge of his nose and down both forearms. A short silver down lies along his forearms and nape, flattening into fine silver streaks when the wind presses on it. His ears tip outward when he smiles. A warm, earnest air.
build: about 182 cm, tall, lean and long-limbed, a distance runner's build with long legs.
palette: sand gold and silver grey, warm amber, faded indigo, a little brass
casual: His courier's road clothes: a long sand-coloured hooded cloak thrown back, dusty at the hem; under it a faded indigo linen tunic belted at the waist, a sand-coloured scarf loose at the throat, close-fitting trousers tucked into soft tall riding boots; a worn leather letter satchel across his body, its flap stamped with a small post-horn mark; the long single-edged courier's sabre at his left hip in a plain leather scabbard. He holds the edge of the cloak in one hand, about to shake the sand out of it, the ears tipped outward, a sheepish, friendly smile.
private: At the wind-worn post station after the riders are in: a loose undyed linen shirt with the sleeves pushed up, a sleeveless felt vest, soft trousers, bare feet, the tail curled round. He holds a sealed letter up close, frowning at the name on it, the ears pricked. An earnest, puzzled look.
battle: Holding open the crack in the storm, in the lightest top-grade gear of a legend who lives by speed: a fitted coat of small sand-gold scales cut from deep-floor beast hide and riveted with pale mountain copper, each scale etched with a wind rune that glows a soft amber; a sand-coloured enchanted cloak whose hem ripples with a faint silver wind-light; slim engraved bracers and greaves of dark blued steel; the sand scarf pulled up over the nose; the letter satchel strapped tight to his back. He holds the long single-edged courier's sabre, its blade gently curved, its brass knuckle-bow guard Western-style, out in front of him in both hands, a thin blade of clear starlit light opening along its edge and splitting the swirling sand around him. The silver down on his forearms flattened into glowing streaks, the ears back, the amber eyes fierce.
formal: At the post station on the day the riders give a name to the road: a clean dark indigo wool riding coat closed down the front with brass buttons, fitted sleeves, a sand-gold sash, a polished brass post-horn badge on the breast, the sand-coloured cloak brushed clean, tall boots polished, the sabre at his hip. He stands very upright with the hands folded in front, the ears up, a shy, serious look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the amber eyes looking at the viewer with a wide, earnest smile, the ears tipped outward, one hand pushing the hood back. Low gold desert sunset light from one side and a wall of blowing sand on the other, a narrow clear strip of starlit sky showing through it. Foreground blur: drifting sand, the broken half of a long blade and a letter's wax seal. He wears the sand-coloured hooded cloak over the indigo tunic.

Mist-blue hair cut straight at the jaw. Sea-green eyes. Thick calluses across the heels of both palms from pressing on stone. On long trips she carries a small soft pillow her mother sewed from an old faded rose-print skirt, a family mark stitched in one corner. A cheerful, practical, warm air; she always goes round to look at the other side before she calls anything safe.
build: about 168 cm, sturdy and strong: square flat shoulders, a medium bust, a firm waist and solid hips, strong legs.
palette: mist blue and sea green, earth ochre, slate grey, faded rose

She has one calloused hand on the pack strap and the other half raised as if to point at the far side of something, a bright, curious look.
private: At home with the Hessinger family: a loose cream linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up, a knitted sea-green cardigan, a long brown wool skirt, soft shoes, the hair tucked behind one ear. battle: Raising the dike in the mine tunnel, in the top-grade field gear of a legend who works with her hands on stone: the long slate-grey coat lined with small overlapping plates of enchanted grey stone-scale that glow along their seams with an earth-yellow light; a fitted mountain-copper half-cuirass etched with academy rune lines; heavy mountain-copper gauntlets left open at the palms so her calloused hands touch the stone; a small cast war badge of shield, broken sword and banner at the breast; the small pillow tied at the back of her belt. Feet braced, jaw set, the sea-green eyes steady.
formal: The day the guild's register first wrote her name: a clean slate-blue wool coat closed down the front with plain bronze buttons, fitted sleeves, over a white shirt with a soft collar, an ochre sash, the boots scrubbed, the mist-blue hair combed neat. She stands very upright with the hands folded in front, trying not to grin, a bright, slightly embarrassed look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the sea-green eyes looking at the viewer with a reassuring smile, one calloused palm raised toward the viewer as if about to press it on stone. Pale grey marsh-fog light from one side and a warm earth-yellow glow rising from her hand on the other. Foreground blur: drifting fog, a rising wet block of old dike stone set with shells, and an old iron nail.

A white, glossy old burn scar from the back of her right hand up the forearm (on the viewer's left when she faces us). Her smith's hammer has five strips of different cloth wound round its handle. art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face turned slightly, the ice-blue eyes looking down at glowing metal just out of frame, sparks crossing the frame.
